items.title: Jason Arday: Ex-Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism scandal found dead
items.summary: Jason Arday, the youngest ever Black professor at Cambridge, was found unresponsive at an address in London. Arday had recently resigned in the midst of a plagiarism row.

items.title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty to federal stalking charges in Brian Thompson death
items.summary: The plea resolves the remaining federal charges tied to the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson and could affect a separate New York state case.

items.title: Taliban pressured by insurgents after 5 years in power
items.summary: The Taliban managed to retake power in Afghanistan on August 15, 2021. Now, they face armed factions who challenge the Taliban rule and strain their central claim of providing security.

items.title: Congo's Ebola cases rising at record pace
items.summary: The Ebola virus is spreading rapidly in the DRC. In Kinshasa, a city of millions, fears of a serious health crisis are growing. Hospitals are scrambling to prepare for emergencies as best as they can.

items.title: Can a giant Madonna help slow secularization in Poland?
items.summary: Europe's largest statue of the Virgin Mary will be inaugurated on Saturday in the Polish village of Konotopie. What will the monument mean for the village it towers over — and for the Catholic faith in Poland?

items.title: Romania shuts nuclear plant, Hungary dams dry Danube River
items.summary: Romania has shut down its only nuclear plant in a rare move prompted by the lack of cooling water from the Danube River. Hungary, meanwhile, is racing to dam the Danube, trying to keep its Paks plant online.

items.title: Kennedy Center board approves Trump name on facade, renovation plan
items.summary: The move appears designed to circumvent a judge's ruling that the US president's name should be removed, potentially setting the stage for a new legal fight over the Kennedy Center's name and future.

items.title: After Women in India Joined Protests, Online Harassment Followed
items.summary: Widespread online abuse and visits from the police show the added risks women take standing up for their beliefs in a patriarchal society.

items.title: With Priests Scarce in Rural Italy, an African Pastor Is Filling the Void
items.summary: Immigrants have long eased labor shortages on farms and factories in Italy. But churches also need foreign-born priests, like the Rev. Vincent Souly of the Ivory Coast.

items.title: Professor’s Death Leaves Behind Hard Questions for Cambridge on Race and Hiring
items.summary: Jason Arday, the school’s youngest Black professor, was found dead on Friday. The school ignored a series of warnings about his life story and his work.

items.title: The Iranian YouTube Show Posing Questions Few Dare Ask
items.summary: Azad, a popular online debate program, has tackled topics that push the limits of Iran’s authoritarian system. Some question how it has remained on air.

items.title: Syrian Convicted in Austria of Civil War Abuses Is Detained in Syria
items.summary: Musab Abu Rukbah, a former police chief, left Austria after appealing his eight-year sentence for crimes committed during Syria’s civil war.

items.title: Canadian Petition to Expel U.S. Ambassador Pete Hoekstra Takes Off
items.summary: Mr. Hoekstra has been President Trump’s faithful messenger in Canada amid a historic low in relations. More than 170,000 Canadians want him gone.

items.title: $10 Million in Gold Found Buried Under Former Brewery in Belgium
items.summary: A construction worker’s drill struck gold during a renovation project in East Flanders, setting off a search for the owners of the stashed fortune.

items.title: Wary of Trump, Europe Seeks Role in Eventual Russia-Ukraine Talks
items.summary: French, German and British diplomats are working on a format for future negotiations — even if Russia has shown little interest.

items.title: Iran Says Qatar Captured Its Pilots Months Ago, a Claim Qatar Rejects
items.summary: Iran said the airmen have been held since March 2 when their fighter jets were shot down. The Qatari government denies detaining any Iranian pilots.

items.title: Israeli Strikes in Lebanon Kill 11, Health Officials Say
items.summary: The Lebanese health ministry said children were among those killed. The Israeli prime minister’s office said Hezbollah had struck first, injuring three Israeli soldiers.

items.title: At Least 47 Dead as 7.7-Magnitude Earthquake Rocks Indonesia
items.summary: The temblor was one of the strongest the area had experienced in decades, an official said.

items.title: Entrenched, Embattled and Defiant, the Taliban Celebrate 5 Years in Power
items.summary: The Taliban have Afghanistan in a chokehold that spares no one. But threats are starting to crack their veneer of stability and control.

items.title: Heat Deaths in a ‘Cold’ Country Are a Warning to the Rest of Europe
items.summary: A June heat wave in Belgium and neighboring countries exposed a lethal lack of readiness. That’s a risk as another wave hits Europe.

items.title: Russia Campaigned to Derail Moldova’s Pro-Western Government
items.summary: In Moldova, Moscow paid Orthodox priests, conducted a vote-buying scheme and set up training camps on election interference — all in an effort to derail the Western-leaning government.

items.title: Jason Arday, Cambridge Professor Accused of Plagiarism, Is Found Dead
items.summary: Mr. Arday resigned last week after the university announced an investigation into allegations of plagiarism and fabrication.

items.title: Bou Meng, Rare Survivor of Khmer Rouge Torture House, Dies at 85
items.summary: Saved by his ability to paint, he was one of only a handful of prisoners to make it out of the brutal prison Tuol Sleng.

items.title: Quit Lit
items.summary: There are good reasons to abandon books we’re not enjoying, but our attenuated attention might lead us to tap out too early.

items.title: Summer Camps Strive to Stay Part of Canadian Life, Despite Hurdles
items.summary: Long a tradition for many kids and teenagers across the country, overnight camps are facing financial and cultural hurdles as inflation bites and parenting trends shift.

items.title: How Cyclospora Evaded the U.S. Food Safety System to Sicken Thousands
items.summary: The Trump administration delayed a rule last year that could have sped up the effort to pinpoint the source of the contamination. Critics charge that food safety oversight has eroded overall.

items.title: As China Pushes to Expand in Asia, Trump Focuses on Iran
items.summary: Asian allies are beginning to wonder whether the United States would or could defend them in a war.

items.title: Where Future Champions Race Against the Tide
items.summary: An uninhabited Irish island fills up one day each summer for a treasured amateur horse race in which young jockeys ride across the shifting sands.

items.title: Where to Eat and Drink at a Barcelona Bar Like a Local
items.summary: The classic bars, known as bodegas, are where locals in the Catalan capital take their rituals seriously. If you know where to look, you can join them.

items.title: As Army Fails to Protect Palestinians, Israeli Leaders Sympathize With Settlers
items.summary: Defense Minister Katz called for the military to turn over to the police the responsibility for protecting Palestinians after two West Bank families were besieged by violent settlers.

items.title: When a Rare Wolf Got Too Close, Denmark Faced a Conservation Dilemma
items.summary: The authorities tracked the animal after a string of close encounters with residents, reigniting a bitter debate over how a small, densely populated country should live with wolves.

items.title: A Prominent Mexican Politician Says U.S. Revoked His Visa
items.summary: Andrés Manuel López Beltrán, a former president’s son, lashed out at the Trump administration after he said it canceled his visa, another flashpoint in the tense U.S.-Mexico relationship.

items.title: Britain’s Farage Takes a Page From Trump’s Playbook Amid Investigations
items.summary: Nigel Farage, the Reform U.K. leader who resigned from Parliament and won back his seat on Thursday, stays on the offensive and says voters don’t care about allegations of financial impropriety.

items.title: The Taliban Kicked the U.S. Out of Afghanistan. Now They Want It Back.
items.summary: In an interview, Afghanistan’s foreign minister called on the U.S. to reopen its embassy and invest in the country — a near-impossible sell for now, analysts and former diplomats say.

items.title: France’s Top Court Strikes Down Ban on Social Media for Children
items.summary: The move was a setback for President Emmanuel Macron, who championed the ban. He vowed to pass a new version before he leaves office next spring.

items.title: Zambia Halts Presidential Election Vote Count Over Violence and Fraud Allegations
items.summary: The electoral commission for the southern African nation said poll workers had been attacked and ballots had been stolen.

items.title: Five Arrested in Connection to Stolen Works by Cézanne, Renoir and Matisse, Prosecutors Say
items.summary: The Italian military police said that art collectively valued at more than $10 million had been found five months after being taken in a nighttime heist near Parma.

items.title: With Trump’s Hamas Deal in Peril, Kushner Set to Visit Israel for Gaza Talks
items.summary: Jared Kushner, President Trump’s senior aide, is expected to meet with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel, who has rejected a U.S.-backed deal to disarm Hamas.

items.title: Heat Is Hammering Europe, Again. Here’s What That Looks Like.
items.summary: Extreme temperatures and repeated wildfires are pushing infrastructure to the limit and testing the continent’s resolve.

items.title: 8 Matisse Works, Looted from Library in Brazil, Are Recovered
items.summary: The prints by the French master were taken in São Paulo last year in a brazen daylight heist.

items.title: Kevin Rideout, American Missionary Kidnapped in Niger, Is Released
items.summary: Kevin Rideout, a pilot, was abducted from his home in the country’s capital, Niamey, last fall. His mission organization said he was in “good health” after his release.

items.title: Record-Breaking Rainfall Leaves Eight Dead and Thousands Stranded in Japan
items.summary: Three months’ worth of rain fell in just 12 hours in a region east of Tokyo, leading to deadly flooding.

items.title: Palestinian Rappers Shabjdeed and Saint Levant in Spat Over Authenticity
items.summary: Shabjdeed, a rapper in the West Bank, criticized a fellow Palestinian musician in a song, saying his Western lifestyle and lyrics were far removed from life back home.

items.title: After Notre-Dame Fire, France Restored the Cathedral — but Not These Windows
items.summary: France has faithfully renovated most of what burned at Notre-Dame in 2019. Contentiously, six towering windows will soon be replaced by a new design.

items.title: As Europe Gets Hotter, Its Transportation Systems Struggle to Cope
items.summary: The continent’s railways and roads “were engineered for a climate that no longer exists,” one expert said.

items.title: Farage Wins Special U.K. Election That He Initiated, as Expected
items.summary: Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform U.K., won the Clacton by-election with 63 percent. Count Binface, a novelty candidate, came second with 27 percent, a personal best.

items.title: Will Sudan’s El Obeid Become the Next El Fasher? What to Know.
items.summary: Taking El Obeid would allow the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces to consolidate its hold on western Sudan, a significant strategic goal.

items.title: After 2 Plasma Donor Deaths, Company Pauses Clinics in Canada
items.summary: Grifols, a Spanish company, said “unfounded attention” on its blood plasma business in Canada had led it to temporarily end collections at 17 clinics.

items.title: Engine Blade Hit Window on Jet Before Man Was Partly Sucked Outside, Report Says
items.summary: The National Transportation Safety Board said it had found a bird’s remains and feathers on a broken engine.

items.title: Afghan Women Erased From Public Life in Five Years of Taliban Rule
items.summary: Decrees restricting the rights of women and girls to study, work, travel and act independently now threaten to damage Afghanistan permanently, experts say.

items.title: Electric Thrills
items.summary: Electric motorcycle sales are surging in Pakistan, as wartime prices accelerate the pivot away from fossil fuels in the developing world.

items.title: Israeli Settlers Resume West Bank Siege After Eviction
items.summary: The military’s failure to keep extremists away from two Palestinian families trapped in their West Bank homes made clear the chaos gripping the Israeli-occupied territory.

items.title: Early-Onset El Niño
items.summary: The global weather disrupter appears to be taking a toll, and its peak could still be months away.

items.title: Train Derails Near Town of Lewes in East Sussex, U.K.
items.summary: Emergency services said they were working at the scene of a derailment near Lewes, in East Sussex, on Thursday. Eighteen other people were less badly hurt.

items.title: Topos Azteca, a Mexican Volunteer Rescue Group, Helps With Rescue Efforts After Colombia Earthquake
items.summary: Topos Azteca, a Mexican volunteer rescue group that works worldwide and helped after the Sept. 11 attacks, arrived in Colombia after searching for survivors in Venezuela.

items.title: Brazil’s Disease-Fighting Mosquitoes
items.summary: Our reporter, Apoorva Mandavilli, goes inside a mosquito factory in Brazil, where scientists are producing millions of mosquitoes to fight deadly tropical diseases in a warming world.

items.title: A City Mobilizes Against a Stubborn Health Threat: Mosquitoes
items.summary: The city of Belém in northern Brazil was overwhelmed by an outbreak of dengue two years ago. An all-out municipal effort has reduced cases and may offer lessons to American cities.

items.title: How a Long-Shot U.S. Oil Drilling Project Is Shaking Up Greenland
items.summary: A U.S. oil company says it could be on the verge of a major discovery in Greenland. The proposal comes at a tricky time for the Arctic island, and locals are lining up against it.

items.title: Former Catholic Bishop Is Convicted of Sexual Abuse, Australian News Outlets Say
items.summary: A court found Christopher Alan Saunders, the former bishop of Broome, guilty of sexually abusing two men, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation reported.

items.title: Hundreds of Flights Canceled in Sicily as Mount Etna Erupts
items.summary: Etna erupts often, but it usually doesn’t release this much ash, an expert said. Tens of thousands of travelers’ plans have been disrupted in the past week.
